item.title: By: Jack Heath
item.dc:creator: Jack Heath
item.description: This issue was related to the system not reading the correct encoding for the file. It was a common bug in 2003 which may carry over to Outlook 2007/2010 emails sent from an unpatched 2003 client in text format. To resolve it, I just opened an email (any email will work) and added then encoding option to the quick-bar, then I selected UTF-8 as an encoding option. Once done, Outlook will add UTF-8 to the list and be able to autos-elect between both UTF-Western and UTF-8 formats.

item.title: By: Jorrit Schippers
item.dc:creator: Jorrit Schippers
item.description: This article suggests that Outlook 2003 is incapable of accepting UTF-8 messages. This is not true. It might be a component between the originating mailserver and Outlook that mangles the contents, as I have experienced myself. To be on the safe side, use Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable (and encode the contents accordingly)
